title: His hope to teach again and what he now knows about music
summary: Without a degree, he plans to approach colleges and says he could have been a great arranger had he known earlier.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: But I'm trying to find out where you are, in your story. We've talked about all of these people who have come through your life. But Walter, what is the assets of Walter?

Well, the biggest aspiration I've got now is maybe to try to teach. But my only holdback on that is that I don't have a college degree. But as soon as I get some things straightened out, I'm going to make a resume of myself and send it out to a few of the colleges. I like to teach students.
Well, in this day and times now, the educational system has given us what we call lifetime experiences for people like you that have spent a certain

length of time and lived their lifetime in this business... They give you credit for that, I guess what they would call a degree, since they would know that if you had spent the time in school that you spent outside preparing yourself for the world in which you were (?). In many cases, you don't need degrees for people like you to share your expertise with the young people.
And they certainly need you. But what I'm trying to follow is, would you say you want to come back to music now after experiencing all of that booking agent experience, of managing other people?

Yes. I'll tell you, there's so many things that's come to me in music, I think it would be a great thing if the youngsters could find it out now. It took me a lifetime to find it out. Just from my reviewing of the things I did with Timothy and the writings I did... I found out so many things that was a short... Let me put it this way. If I had known some of these things years ago, I could have been a great writer-arranger. And I was fairly good, but was not knowing what I know then. Because I think back on some of the arrangements I made, and they were good. But after I studied, I really got the science of it. Because I remember years ago, I heard guys come out of college who
couldn't arrange. I arranged before I even studied. But I wasn't arranging that good. There are certain secrets... There are certain little secrets about music...

But are you willing to say now, to admit that in your life cycle, that your ability to go from one thing to another, and still to have the stick-to-it-iveness thing after going through what you did to learn the instrumentation...
